description: Evaluates Stage 1 User Goals Portfolio & Journey Prioritization

evals.prompt: I am building an airline ticketing website. Help me create my portfolio of user goals for WebMCP.
evals.expected_output: Prioritized candidate user goals with defined outcomes, required context, and boundaries for each goal, followed by offering the developer a choice between Interactive Mode (stepping through Stages 2–4 one goal at a time with developer checkpoints) and Autonomous Mode (the agent working through Stages 2–6 end-to-end without intermediate stops).
assertions: The agent proposes prioritized candidate user goals (such as flight search, seat selection, booking, or check-in)
The agent defines outcomes, required context, or boundaries for each proposed goal

The agent offers the developer a choice between Interactive Mode (stepping through Stages 2–4 one goal at a time with developer checkpoints) and Autonomous Mode (having the agent work through Stages 2–6 end-to-end without intermediate stops)

evals.prompt: We identified 5 user goals for our app (search products, view cart, checkout, apply coupon, track order). Can you simulate and role-play all 5 goals in bulk in a single turn right now?
evals.expected_output: The agent explains that each goal must be isolated and go through its full Stages 2–4 cycle (starting states, turn-by-turn role-play, variations, and critique of agent demeanor, clarifying questions, and autonomous confirmation boundaries) rather than mashing all 5 goals into a single superficial bulk turn. It offers Interactive Mode (stepping through one goal at a time with developer critique) or Autonomous Mode (where the agent works through each isolated goal's Stages 2–4 and self-critique sequentially without stopping for developer questions).
assertions: The agent explains that each goal must be isolated and go through its full Stages 2–4 cycle (starting states, turn-by-turn role-play, variations, and critique) rather than mashing all 5 goals into a single superficial bulk simulation
The agent mentions evaluating agent demeanor/tone, clarifying questions, and autonomous confirmation boundaries for each goal

The agent offers the choice between Interactive Mode (reviewing one goal at a time with developer critique) and Autonomous Mode (having the agent work through each isolated goal's Stages 2–4 and self-critique sequentially without intermediate stops)
